executive_summary: SonicWave's subscriber base shows an overall monthly churn rate of 9.71%, putting $9,162.75 in monthly recurring revenue at risk across 8,500 subscribers. Churn risk is heavily concentrated within two specific interaction segments rather than distributed across broad customer categories: subscribers with repeated billing support inquiries (S2) and low-usage Premium subscribers acquired via partner promotions (S1). Together, segments S1 and S2 account for only 11.8% of subscribers but generate 72.2% ($6,618.69) of all monthly revenue at risk. Conversely, the remaining 7,496 subscribers in baseline segment S3 churn at a healthy 3.14%, meaning broad retention discounts would be wasteful. Our strategy prioritizes resolving recurring billing friction and restructuring partner promo onboarding, with controlled A/B experiments before any permanent rollout.

segment_plans.priority_rationale: S2 represents the largest revenue exposure in the company, with $4,073.91 in monthly revenue at risk (44.46% of total at-risk revenue) across 682 subscribers and 383.5 expected churners. Because this risk is driven by operational friction in customer support and billing resolution, it is immediately addressable by internal workflow improvements.
segment_plans.root_cause_hypothesis: Subscribers experiencing unresolved billing discrepancies who must open two or more support tickets encounter customer service fatigue and cancel out of frustration rather than dissatisfaction with the music service itself.
evidence: Segment S2 has an actual churn rate of 56.45% (predicted 56.23%), representing a 5.79x lift vs overall churn.
Chart 02 shows that when last ticket topic is Billing, churn is only 5% with 1 ticket (n=847), but jumps to 57% at 2 tickets (n=547) and 53% at 3+ tickets (n=135).
The interaction flag for Billing with 2+ tickets carries an odds ratio of 33.833 in the logistic regression model.
Monthly revenue at risk for S2 is $4,073.91 out of $7,242.07 total segment monthly revenue.

actions.title: Establish Priority Billing Resolution Queue
actions.description: Automatically route any customer who opens a second billing ticket within 90 days to a dedicated Tier-2 billing specialist team with authority to issue immediate credits. Ensure proactive outbound phone or chat follow-up within 24 hours to confirm the issue is fully solved.
actions.kpi: First-contact resolution rate on second billing tickets and 60-day post-ticket churn rate

actions.title: Implement Self-Service Invoice and Subscription Audit
actions.description: Deploy an in-app billing dashboard clarification tool showing line-item subscription charges, renewal dates, and payment history to prevent repetitive customer queries. Add automatic charge notifications before subscription renewals take place.
actions.kpi: Volume of repeat billing tickets within 90 days

experiment.hypothesis: Providing dedicated senior billing escalation with one-touch resolution on a user's second billing ticket will reduce 90-day churn by at least 20% relative to standard routing.
experiment.design: Randomize subscribers submitting a 2nd billing ticket in 90 days into two equal cohorts of 341 subscribers: Control receives standard support queue routing; Treatment receives immediate routing to specialized senior agents with pre-authorized credit discretion. Monitor across 60 days.
experiment.success_metric: 30-day and 60-day subscriber churn rate post-ticket resolution.

segment_plans.priority_rationale: S1 has the highest churn rate in the company (actual 63.66%, predicted 60.84%) and accounts for $2,544.78 in monthly revenue at risk across 322 subscribers (27.77% of all at-risk revenue). While highly acute, it ranks second to S2 due to smaller total subscriber count and lower overall revenue exposure.
segment_plans.root_cause_hypothesis: Subscribers acquired through external partner promotions on Premium plans who fail to build regular listening habits view the recurring Premium price as unjustifiable once introductory promotional periods expire.
evidence: Segment S1 churns at 63.66% actual (60.84% predicted) with a 6.27 lift versus overall company churn.
The model indicates an odds ratio of 47.983 for the combination of Premium + Low-usage + Partner promo.
Chart 04 reveals that Low-usage subscribers acquired via Partner promo churn at 52% (n=435), whereas Partner promo users with Balanced, Music-heavy, or Podcast-heavy mixes churn at only 7%.
Chart 03 shows Premium Low-usage churn is 37% (n=666), compared to 7-8% for other content mixes on Premium.
Expected monthly revenue at risk is $2,544.78 across 195.9 expected churners.

actions.title: Launch Partner Promo Onboarding & Habit Activation
actions.description: Trigger a targeted 14-day progressive onboarding sequence for partner promo signups featuring personalized playlist imports and weekly curated mixes to increase active listening days. Use SMS and push nudges highlighting offline downloads and podcast exclusives.
actions.kpi: Weekly active days and percentage of users graduating out of Low-usage content mix

actions.title: Pre-Renewal Downsell & Plan Flexibility Option
actions.description: For partner promo Premium users who remain in the Low-usage tier near month 11 (median tenure 11.0 months), offer a proactive downgrade path to the Basic tier or an annual discount before cancellation occurs.
actions.kpi: Paid retention rate at promo conversion/anniversary

experiment.hypothesis: Delivering an active onboarding sequence with personalized playlist curation will increase engagement and reduce churn among partner promo Premium subscribers by at least 20%.
experiment.design: Split 320 newly identified or eligible partner promo Premium low-usage subscribers 50/50: Control receives standard marketing emails; Treatment receives the tailored playlist setup and habit-forming notification flow over 30 days.
experiment.success_metric: Share of subscribers remaining active at 60 days and churn rate differential between cohorts.

segment_plans.priority_rationale: S3 covers 7,496 subscribers (88.19% of the base) and has a low churn rate of 3.14% actual (3.31% predicted). Because churn here represents natural baseline turnover, invasive or expensive retention interventions would erode margin without providing incremental lift.
segment_plans.root_cause_hypothesis: Churn in this cohort reflects standard background attrition (payment expiries, platform switching, natural life events) rather than systemic product or support dissatisfaction.
evidence: Actual churn rate is 3.14% (predicted 3.31%), with a lift of 0.34 vs overall churn.
Median tenure is 12.0 months, support tickets in 90 days median is 0.0, and average weekly hours median is 8.0.
Generates $77,621.28 in monthly revenue, representing the vast bulk of business cash flow.

actions.title: Automate Smart Dunning and Card Expiry Messaging
actions.description: Implement automated pre-dunning card expiration alerts and account updater protocols to prevent involuntary churn from expired payment cards. Ensure smooth background updates without interrupting user listening sessions.

experiment.hypothesis: Proactive automated reminders for credit cards expiring within 30 days will reduce involuntary background churn by 5%.
experiment.design: A/B test across 2,000 baseline subscribers with upcoming payment card expiration: Control receives standard failed-payment notifications after decline; Treatment receives pre-decline in-app renewal reminders 14 days prior.
experiment.success_metric: Payment renewal success rate and 30-day billing-related churn.

chart_observations.observation: While Support tickets 90d (39% churn for 2, 37% for 3+), Last ticket topic = Billing (28%), Content mix = Low-usage (23%), and Signup channel = Partner promo (22%) show massive raw churn, Plan type = Premium shows 13% and Avg weekly hours shows modest variations (9-12%). The caveats show that individual raw churn rates are misleading because baseline rates outside the high-risk segments drop to ~3%.

This heatmap demonstrates that ticket topic alone does not cause high churn: Billing with 1 ticket has an entirely baseline churn rate of 5% (n=847), but abruptly escalates to 57% (n=547) at 2 tickets and 53% (n=135) at 3+ tickets. Account, Content, and Playback tickets remain between 5% and 10% churn even at 2 tickets, showing that the interaction of Billing and repeated contacts is uniquely toxic.

Low-usage content mix only drives churn when paired with Premium plans (37% churn, n=666). For Free (7%, n=143), Basic (7%, n=304), and Family (7%, n=164), Low-usage churn remains identical to baseline listening groups.

Partner promo signups only exhibit high churn when combined with Low-usage content mix (52% churn, n=435). Partner promo signups who maintain Balanced (7%, n=260), Music-heavy (7%, n=394), or Podcast-heavy (7%, n=191) habits churn at the same 6-8% baseline as Web, iOS, and Android acquisitions.

Interaction features dominate churn odds: Premium + Low-usage + Partner promo raises odds by 47.98x, and Billing + support tickets 90d >= 2 raises odds by 33.83x. Individual ticket categories without repeat tickets show minor odds ratios (Account x1.32, Content x1.29, Billing x1.27), confirming that single isolated features do not explain the risk.

Although S1 has the highest predicted churn rate (61% vs 56% for S2), S2 represents 44% ($4,074) of total expected revenue at risk compared to 28% ($2,545) in S1. S3 contributes 28% of revenue at risk despite a 3% churn rate due to its 7,496 subscriber base.

what_not_to_do: Do not offer blanket retention discounts to all Premium subscribers: outside segments S1 and S2, Premium churn is 3.1%, virtually identical to the 3.1% baseline.

Do not target all Partner promo subscribers with interventions: Partner promo subscribers with Balanced, Music-heavy, or Podcast-heavy listening churn at normal baseline rates of 7%, matching other channels.
Do not intervene after a single billing ticket: subscribers with exactly 1 billing ticket churn at only 5%, which is below the overall average churn rate.
Do not target all Low-usage subscribers indiscriminately: on Basic, Free, and Family plans, Low-usage users churn at normal baseline rates of 7%, close to the general 3.1% non-segment baseline.
Do not launch high-cost loyalty or content perks for baseline Segment S3: S3 already exhibits very low churn (3.14%), making expensive retention efforts margin-dilutive.
risks_and_caveats: Identified churn drivers represent statistical associations from historical data rather than proven causal relationships; interventions must be tested via randomized trials before full implementation.

Raw single-attribute churn rates for Premium (13%), Low-usage (23%), Billing (28%), and Partner promo (22%) are explained by the interaction segments S1 and S2; outside these segments, those groups churn at ~2.9% to 3.4%.
Subscribers who meet criteria for both interaction terms have overlapping rather than additive risks, requiring model corrections to avoid double-counting.
Savings estimates rely on conservative assumed churn reductions (0.05 to 0.20) and require validation through empirical A/B test results.
